clues.title: Plate: blue strips both sides, short front
text: Contrary to most European licence plates, Italian plates have blue strips on **either side** of the plate. Furthermore, the front plate is distinctly **shorter** than most European plates, which in combination with the two strips, makes it unique.
NOTE: Albanian licence plates also have two blue strips, and French licence plates have a smaller strip on the right. However, neither Albanian nor French front plates are short.

images.caption: Italian plates: short front (top) and long rear (bottom)

clues.summary: Blue strips on both sides of the plate, and a front plate noticeably shorter than most European ones. Together that is unique. Albania has two strips but long front plates.

differs.how: Two blue strips but front plates are not short
Only a small strip on the right, front not short

clues.title: Bollard: triangular, black top, red front reflector
text: Italian bollards are triangular in shape, and white with a **black top**. They have a red front and a white rear reflector.
NOTE: Albania uses the same bollards.
clues.summary: White triangular bollard with a black top, a red reflector at the front and a white one at the back. Albania uses the same one.

clues.title: Road lines: white solid edges, no centre line
text: One of the most common types of Italian road lines are **white solid outer lines** with no middle line. This is generally less common in other Mediterranean countries.
clues.summary: Very common: solid white edge lines with no middle line. Less common in other Mediterranean countries.

clues.title: Language: double consonants, many i, vowel endings
text: Italian is the most spoken language in Italy. It uses many double consonants, and typically has a very large number of i’s. You can also find ì, é and à. Most words will end with a vowel.
NOTE: The Italian word for street is ‘via’, and can be found on most street signs.
clues.summary: Lots of double consonants and many letter i, plus ì, é and à. Most words end in a vowel. Street signs usually say via.

clues.title: Landscape: farmland on rolling hills, forested valleys
text: Italy has a **Mediterranean landscape** with a lot of agricultural fields on rolling hills, and forested mountain valleys.
clues.summary: A Mediterranean look: farm fields on rolling hills and forested mountain valleys.

clues.title: Houses: pastel stone, terracotta roofs, split shutters
text: Italian architecture mainly consists of pastel coloured stone houses, generally with terracotta roofs. Houses will very commonly have wooden shutters, which will typically be divided in two and open sideways.
clues.summary: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs. Wooden shutters are very common and split in two, opening sideways.

clues.title: Pole: round concrete
text: Unlike most Mediterranean countries, Italy features a lot of **round concrete poles**.
clues.summary: Lots of round concrete poles, which most other Mediterranean countries do not have.

clues.title: Pole: wooden with small white sticker
text: Wooden poles in Italy will commonly feature a small **white pole sticker**.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on a small white sticker on the wooden pole

clues.summary: Wooden poles often carry a small white sticker.

clues.title: Pole: concrete trident tops
text: The most common pole tops in Italy are **concrete trident pole tops**.
There are several possible configurations of insulators.The two shown in the image are the most common ones.
clues.summary: The most common pole top is a concrete trident, with a few possible insulator layouts. The two in the picture are the most common.

clues.title: Guardrail: double guardrails
text: It is very common to find **double guardrails** in Italy.
clues.summary: Double guardrails, with two rails stacked, are very common.

clues.title: Guardrail: red front reflectors
text: Italian guardrails feature **red** front reflectors.
NOTE: This is most useful to distinguish Italy from Spain, which uses yellow reflectors. For a good overview of European guardrails, see [this infographic](/images/italy/europeguardrail.png).
clues.summary: Guardrails have red reflectors on the front. This mainly separates it from Spain, which uses yellow.

clues.title: Guardrail: end flattens, widens, bends away
text: Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape. The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.
clues.summary: Guardrail ends get flatter and wider and bend away from the road.

clues.title: Sign: black or dark grey backs
text: It is very common for the back of Italian road signs to be **black**, or dark grey.
clues.summary: The back of road signs is very often black or dark grey.

clues.title: Sign: blue direction sign, white arrow, capitals
text: Directional signs are **blue** with a **white arrow**. All letters on these signs will be **capitalised**.
clues.summary: Blue direction signs with a white arrow. All letters are capitals.

clues.title: Sign: blue national road sign, green on highways
text: Directional signs in national roads (Strada Statale) are **blue** with a **white and blue border**.
Divided highways (Autostrade) have **green** signs with a **white and green border**.
clues.summary: National roads have blue direction signs with a white-and-blue border. Motorways have green signs with a white-and-green border.

clues.title: Marker: white square, roman numeral over number
text: Italian kilometre markers are white squares with a **roman numeral** on top and an arabic numeral on the bottom. The arabic numeral gives you the number of kilometres and the roman numeral gives you the number of hundred metres from the start of the road.
clues.summary: A white square km marker with a roman numeral on top and a regular number below. The number is kilometres; the roman numeral is hundreds of metres.

clues.title: Sign: road numbers start with SS, SR or SP
text: Italian road numbers will normally begin with the letters “SS”, “SR” or “SP”.
The second letter can be used to identify the type of road.
- "S" when it is a State road, so the number is unique within the country.
- "R" when it is a Regional road, so the number is unique to the region.
- "P" when it is a Provincial road, so the number is unique to the province.
clues.summary: Road numbers usually begin with SS (state), SR (regional) or SP (provincial). The second letter shows the road type.

clues.title: Chevron: white arrows on black
text: Italian chevrons are **white arrows** on a **black background**.
NOTE: In Southern Europe, white on black chevrons can also be found in Spain, Greece and Albania.
clues.summary: White arrows on a black background. Spain, Greece and Albania use the same in southern Europe.

clues.title: Sign: white street sign, thin blue border
text: Street signs are typically white with a thin **blue border** and **black text**.
clues.summary: Street signs are usually white with a thin blue border and black text.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, 5 stripes, no belt
text: Italian pedestrian signs have **five stripes** and a basic person without a belt.
clues.summary: Pedestrian sign with five stripes and a basic figure without a belt.

clues.title: Sign: no-parking sign saying "passo carrabile"
text: These signs, featuring a “no parking”-sign with the text “**passo carrabile**” are commonly found in urban areas. At the top of these signs you will typically find the municipality (comune) name.
clues.summary: A no-parking sign with the words passo carrabile (driveway), common in towns. The top usually shows the municipality name.

clues.title: Google car: low Gen 4 smallcam, big round blur
text: Italy has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

clues.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur at the bottom and a small bump at the front. The blur can be transparent and hard to spot.

clues.title: Phone numbers: first area-code digit rises east then south
text: Italian **area codes** follow a pattern where the first digit generally increases to the east, then south.
clues.summary: The first digit of the area code generally increases going east, then south.

clues.title: Flags: every region has its own flag
text: Each Italian region has its own unique flag.

images.caption: Flags of the Italian regions, each labelled with its region name

clues.summary: Each region has its own unique flag, which helps place you in a region.

clues.title: Language: German bilingual signs in the north
text: The region of South Tyrol has a German majority, and as such uses **German bilingual signs**.
clues.summary: One northern region has a German majority, so signs are bilingual in German.

clues.title: Language: French on signs, "rue" next to "via"
text: **French** can be seen on signs in the Aosta Valley. Most notably, street signs often use both the Italian word “via” and the French word “rue”.
clues.summary: In the north-west valley, signs show French as well. Street signs often use both via and rue.

clues.title: Landscape: totally flat and hazy
text: The Padan Plain (commonly referred to as Po Valley) can typically be recognized by its complete **flatness**. The plain has some of the worst air quality in Europe, which has led to much of the coverage having a noticeable [haze](https://www.google.com/maps/@44.9090493,11.4587497,3a,52.2y,90.92h,87.93t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1sZK0fGSH3oe3u7ooE8Yt2KA!2e0!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fpanoid%3DZK0fGSH3oe3u7ooE8Yt2KA%26cb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile.gps%26w%3D203%26h%3D100%26yaw%3D81.52424%26pitch%3D0%26thumbfov%3D100!7i16384!8i8192).
clues.summary: A completely flat plain with some of the worst air in Europe, so much of the coverage looks hazy.

clues.title: Landscape: olive groves, bright rock walls, red soil
text: The landscape on the southeastern peninsula surrounding Bari has many **olive plantations**, which are often seen together with **bright** **rock walls**. The dirt in the region typically has a noticeably red colour.
Beware that a similar landscape can also be found in [southeastern Sicily](https://maps.app.goo.gl/aRgNqNdsccanmo3m8).
clues.summary: In the south-east heel, many olive plantations with bright rock walls and noticeably red soil. South-east Sicily looks similar.

clues.title: Landscape: tall wide mountain ranges, deep valleys
text: The alpine region in northern Italy has tall, wide **mountain ranges** and deep valleys.
clues.summary: In the north, tall, wide mountain ranges and deep valleys.

clues.title: Landscape: dry hills, rocky mountains
text: The Sicilian landscape is characterised by an **arid**, hilly agricultural landscape, often combined with **rocky mountains**.
clues.summary: On the large southern island: arid, hilly farmland, often next to rocky mountains.

clues.title: Landscape: grey rocks sticking out of the ground
text: Grey **rocks** sticking up from the ground are commonly found on Sardinia, particularly in the northeast.

NOTE: A similar phenomenon can be seen on [Sicily](https://www.google.com/maps/@37.4586829,14.0819986,3a,42.3y,232.74h,94.42t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sGGxh3x_wUzS4zIyD0PD2mA!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu), however the landscape will typically be much drier than Sardinia.
clues.summary: On the western island, especially the north-east, grey rocks poke out of the ground. Sicily has similar rocks but is much drier.

clues.title: Plants: cacti in the south
text: **Cacti** in Italy are most common in the south, particularly in Sicily, southern Sardinia and the south of Apulia.
clues.summary: Cacti are most common in the south: Sicily, southern Sardinia and the south of Apulia.

clues.title: Plants: citrus plantations in the far south
text: **Citrus plantations** are primarily found on eastern Sicily and the southern tip of Calabria.
clues.summary: Citrus groves are mostly in eastern Sicily and the southern tip of the mainland toe.

clues.title: Crops: rice in the northern plain
text: **Rice** is mainly produced in the western and central parts of Po valley, and less commonly in Sardinia.
clues.summary: Rice grows mainly in the western and central part of the Po valley, and less often in Sardinia.

clues.title: Houses: rough unpainted brown-grey bricks
text: A lot of buildings in and around Tuscany are made of irregular **unpainted brown-grey bricks**.

NOTE: A similar style of architecture can be found in northeastern [Spain](https://www.google.se/maps/@42.1527702,0.814623,3a,75y,79.59h,97.61t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sBIg-H1KNLM2FxWRl-hDEVQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656).
clues.summary: In and around one central region, many buildings use irregular unpainted brown-grey bricks. North-east Spain has a similar style.

clues.title: Houses: big white stone, wooden details
text: **Alpine architecture**, which typically features large buildings with white stone walls and wooden details, are found in the Alpine region.
clues.summary: In the Alps, large buildings with white stone walls and wooden details.

clues.title: Houses: grey uneven bricks, Alpine look
text: Buildings in Aosta Valley are often built with **grey uneven bricks**, with an Alpine look.
NOTE: This can look superficially similar to Andorran architecture.
clues.summary: In the north-west valley, buildings use grey uneven bricks and look Alpine. They can look a bit like Andorran architecture.

clues.title: Houses: solid wooden shutters, black hinges
text: **Solid wooden shutters** with black metal hinges is a common feature in the northeast of Italy, particularly in Veneto.
clues.summary: Solid wooden shutters with black metal hinges are common in the north-east, especially one region.

clues.title: Houses: pale, flat roofs, 2-3 floors
text: Houses in the Apulian region are generally very light coloured, and have **flat roofs**, typically with two to three floors. The architecture is sometimes reminiscent of the Middle East.
clues.summary: In the heel region, very light-coloured houses with flat roofs, two to three floors. Sometimes reminiscent of the Middle East.

clues.title: Houses: round stone cone roofs (trulli)
text: This particular style of roof, called a **trullo**, is unique to the Itria valley in southeastern Italy. It is particularly common in and around the town of [Alberobello](https://goo.gl/maps/DwAPahJnQNW1BMY2A).
clues.summary: This cone-shaped roof style, a trullo, exists only in one valley in the south-east. It is especially common around one town.

clues.title: Language: Slovene bilingual signs near the border
text: Close to the Slovenian border you can find **Slovene bilingual signs**.

images.caption: Blue direction signs with Italian and Slovene town names, Cividale/Čedad and Pulfero/Podbuniesac

clues.summary: Close to the north-eastern border you find signs in both languages, with Slovene as the second.

clues.title: Google car: low camera, long antenna, flag, lake west
text: The Campione d'Italia **exclave** in Switzerland can be recognized by its low camera, having a long antenna and a flag. There is also a body of water to the west.

NOTE: This antenna can also be found in several areas in [Switzerland](https://www.google.com/maps/@45.8917308,9.0384397,3a,38.3y,19.25h,71.73t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s0x8K6Xn3tuFsalTznE_BGw!2e0!7i13312!8i6656).
clues.summary: A small exclave inside Switzerland shows a low camera with a long antenna and a flag, and a lake to the west. Some Swiss areas have the same antenna.

clues.title: Landscape: huge volcano in the distance
text: **Etna**, the tallest volcano in Europe, can be seen rising above the landscape from far away in eastern Sicily.
clues.summary: Europe's tallest volcano towers over the landscape from far away in eastern Sicily.

clues.title: Landscape: volcano to the south or east of a city plain
text: The volcano of **Vesuvius** can often be seen to the south or east from the plains around Naples.
clues.summary: Vesuvius is often seen to the south or east from the plains around Naples.

clues.title: City: canals through most of the city
text: Venice can typically be recognized by its many **canals** running through most of the city.
clues.summary: Canals run through most of the city, so streets are mostly water.

clues.title: Landscape: small mountain-ringed plain, north-south grid
text: Piana del Fùcino is a **small plain** surrounded by mountains in the middle of Italy with a grid of roads going completely **north-to-south**.
clues.summary: A small plain surrounded by mountains in central Italy, with roads in a grid running exactly north-south.

clues.title: Landscape: dark volcanic rock, yellow lichen, cacti
text: The island of Pantelleria is a volcanic island southwest of Sicily. Dark volcanic rocks can be seen in the many rock walls of the island, as well as on some houses. It is fairly common to see **yellow lichen** covering the rocks. The island also has a very large amount of cacti.
clues.summary: A volcanic island south-west of Sicily: dark rock walls and houses, yellow lichen on rocks, and lots of cacti.

clues.title: Landscape: volcanic islands, white villas on slopes
text: The Aeolian islands are a volcanic archipelago north of Sicily. Here you will find a mix of volcanic soil and rocks with mediterranean vegetation, like stone pines or olive trees. Like in Sicily, cacti are fairly common.

In the mountains of the islands it is very common to see [touristic white villas](https://www.google.com/maps/@38.4821375,14.9501444,3a,33.7y,13.97h,96.75t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1shlfKkMyHDc-zTzWKFLh70g!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: A volcanic archipelago north of Sicily with volcanic soil, stone pines, olive trees and cacti. White tourist villas are common in the hills.

clues.title: Landscape: twin volcanoes forming a valley
text: Within the Aeolian islands, Salina can easily be distinguished from the **twin volcanoes** forming a valley across the island.
clues.summary: On one of the volcanic islands, two volcanoes form a valley across the island.

clues.title: Landscape: volcano with white stripe near the top
text: Vulcano is perhaps the most easily recognisable of the Aeolian islands, with its volcano having an almost **white stripe of dirt** following the top of the mountainside. It can typically be spotted from [afar](https://goo.gl/maps/THJBuAvQtzUCYWCZ7) on the island.
clues.summary: A volcano with an almost white stripe of dirt along its upper slope. Easy to spot from afar.

clues.title: Landscape: mountain ridge splitting a flat island
text: The island of Favignana has a distinct topography, with mountains running north to south splitting the island in two.
On both sides of the island you will find flat areas, with many rock walls similar to those found in Bari.
Unlike the other islands near Sicily, Favignana is not volcanic.
clues.summary: Mountains run north to south and split the island in two, with flat areas and rock walls on both sides. Unlike nearby islands it is not volcanic.

clues.title: Google car: gloomy overcast Gen 2
text: The island of San Domino only has **overcast Generation 2** coverage, which mostly looks quite gloomy.
clues.summary: This small island has only overcast Gen 2 coverage, which mostly looks gloomy.

clues.title: Language: useful words (senso unico, piazza, vietato)
text: Here are a few words in Italian that can either help you identify the language quickly, be helpful in region guessing, or just help learn the general feel of the language:
**senso unico** - one way
**di** - of (helps distinguish from other romance)
**castello** - castle
**prezzi** - prices
**piazza** - plaza
**autostrada** - highway
**vietato** - prohibited
**polizia** - police
**sconto** - discount

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Handy words: senso unico (one way), di (of), castello, prezzi (prices), piazza, autostrada (motorway), vietato (forbidden), polizia, sconto (discount).

clues.title: Sign: via, strada, viale, tangenziale
text: Italy typical uses the word "via" on their street signs. Note that "strada" also means street but is the same word in Romanian and used more commonly there.
Here are some similar words:
**strada** - street (used more commonly in rural roads)
**tangenziale** - ring road
**viale** - avenue
**circonvallezione** - ring road

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Street signs mostly say via. Strada also means street and is used on rural roads; viale is avenue and tangenziale is ring road. Romanian uses strada more.

clues.title: Language: vowel endings, -zione, gli, gn, sci
text: In Italian most words end in a vowel. Example exceptions include non, il, per, con, del.
Double consonants (tt, zz, cc, ss, bb, pp, ll, gg, etc.) are frequent.
Word endings: -zione, -tà, -aggio, -mento (careful spanish and portuguese use this too)
Letter sequences: gli, gn, sci.
Features of the language include: ì and à

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Most words end in a vowel and double consonants are common. Look for endings -zione, -tà, -aggio, -mento and letter groups gli, gn, sci.

clues.title: Sign: blue corners outside the white edge
text: Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will **not** have a **white/silver border**. Italy will have **blue corners** visible outside the white edge.

images.caption: Pedestrian crossing signs compared: Italy, Romania, Serbia and Slovenia

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Italy, Romania, Serbia and Slovenia look much alike. Italy shows blue corners outside the white edge, while Romania has no white or silver border.

clues.title: Sign: street sign with unusual font, years below
text: Turin street signs have this unique font, sometimes they also have the date of the years on the bottom.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: One northern city has street signs in a unique font, sometimes with years on the bottom.

clues.title: Sign: street sign with logo top left
text: Bari street signs have this unique logo in the top left.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: One southern port city has street signs with a unique logo in the top left.

clues.title: Sign: street sign with extra name under it
text: Naples street signs have a unique font with an extra name under the street name.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: One southern city has street signs in a unique font with an extra name under the street name.

clues.title: Sign: street sign with 4 dots in each corner
text: Palermo street signs have 4 dots in each corner.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: One Sicilian city has street signs with four dots in each corner.

clues.title: Sign: street sign on 3 small supports
text: Florence street signs are supported by 3 small supports (1 on top, 2 on bottom).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: One Tuscan city has street signs held by 3 small supports: one on top and two at the bottom.

clues.title: Sign: huge street sign, thick frame, roman numerals
text: Rome street signs are by far the most distinct street signs in Italy, their bigger than any other street sign in Italy, they have a very thick frame and the Roman numerals in the top right.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The capital has the most distinctive street signs: bigger than any other, with a very thick frame and roman numerals in the top right.
